turns.message: I prepare 20 tubes per run and have 1200 mm of bench width. Compare an assembled platform with a buildable open-source platform. Explain the tradeoffs and ask for my choice before designing anything.
turns.assistant:
With 20 tubes per run and 1200 mm bench width, here are your two routes:

1) Buy assembled OT-2: faster to deploy, official setup and compatible pipettes/racks, schematic deck layout. Needs 1030 mm total width with clearance, fits your 1200 mm. Tradeoffs: quote needed for price/stock, manual pipette not reusable, no custom arm/cooling integration.

2) Build open-hardware Jubilee: open BOM/fabrication, supports custom pipette + camera concepts, 300x300x300 mm stated volume. Tradeoffs: sourcing, assembly, calibration and liquid validation are on you.

Which do you prefer - assembled OT-2 or buildable Jubilee - before I design anything?

Recorded a 1200 mm maximum width. Develop a fresh layout with Meta to check the arrangement; this message has not generated a new machine.
